key_distinction: REGISTRATION (where the DM chart sits relative to the atlas coast) is what these numbers measure; the RENDERING MEDIUM (raster vs vector) does not change any of them. A vector city placed through the same cityBox carries the same 8.5 atlas px rms coast error.

method.dem: EPESHU_HF_URI decoded from index.html (h=(R*256+G)/32-300 m; same decode as decodeEpeshuHF and tools/filigree-dem.js). Grid to atlas by the sim:S1 formula atlasX=1060+gx*800/768, atlasY=1240+gy*800/768 (vertex convention; sim gridToWorld treats samples as vertices). 0 m contour = sign changes of h between 4-neighbour samples, sub-cell by linear interpolation; sim sea is SEA_Y=0. Sea = h<0 connected to the window border (raw all-h<0 variant differs by <=0.04 px rms). Raw decode: genHydrology carving of W.H is NOT applied (untested).
method.print: z5 tiles maps-site/tiles/5 over window [1060,1860)x[1240,2040) (+20 atlas px pad) through a numpy port of buildCityMask: weight where luma>=110, water where also r-b<=54, separable radius-2 box blur of both, ratio>=0.5, keep only water 4-connected to the patch border. Coast = mask pixel edges (0.5 atlas px). PIL JPEG decode, not the browser's.
method.patch_check: The same port run on sampleCityMask's exact Epeshu patch (ox 2402, oy 2760, n 140 z5 px = atlas [1201,1271]x[1380,1450]) agrees with the window mask on 99.79% of pixels and its coast coincides with the window coast (0.0 px).
method.dm_art: maps-site/art/overlay-Epeshu.jpg 2863x3072; water class = L1 distance to the flat sea fill RGB(119,153,136) < 36 and nearer than the olive countryside RGB(102,119,85), opened 2x, largest component, holes filled (15.5% of pixels are exactly the fill colour; class covers 16.1%). Coast points within 40 art px of the frame dropped. Placed as cityBox does (capital FOOT_R 26, hw=26*2863/3072=24.23, hh=26) times scale s, centre (1236.1+dx, 1415).
method.chamfer: Nearest-point distance with scipy cKDTree. 'a_to_b' queries every a-point against all b-points; window results drop query points within 3 px of the window edge; r60 queries points within 60 atlas px of the anchor (1236.1,1415) against the full-window reference. For the art, print_to_art/dem_to_art query only reference points inside the placed box (shrunk 1 px), so that direction is not comparable across box sizes; art_to_ref is.
method.islet_tiers: raw = masks as built; islets_lt400px2_filled = land components under 400 atlas px2 filled in both masks (mainland coast only). Print water holes from sea lettering and islets have no DEM counterpart and dominate raw print_to_dem.
method.screen_px: screen px = atlas px * 2^(z-4). Epeshu's own deepest atlas zoom is cityMaxZ = min(Z_STREET, 4+log2(3072/52)) = 9.885, so 11.5 is reached only at the street-view handoff, not on the atlas over Epeshu.
method.scripts: throwaway numpy scripts in a mktemp dir (coast.py, refine.py, art2.py); nothing under the repo was written.

window_raw.note: print_to_dem rms/max are sea-lettering holes and islets the DEM lacks (p50 1.84); dem_to_print is the clean reading

window_mainland.note: rms 8.39 / max 54.4 are dominated by the islet-merge filter artefact at (1319,1391); the mainland reading is p50 1.2 / p95 3.64 here and window_raw.dem_to_print rms 1.33.

dem_vs_print.dominant_offset: None worth correcting. Mean nearest vector DEM->print is 0.31 px at 150 deg (SSE) over the window and 0.46 px at 137 deg (SE) within 60 px; the best rigid shift is 1.7-1.8 px toward SSE/S (154-186 deg) and lowers mainland symmetric rms only 1.50->1.02 (r60) and 5.23->5.07 (window). The cell-centre convention (+0.52,+0.52) removes about half of the mean vector. Both coasts agree to about one DEM cell (1.04 px) plus the print coast stroke, which the anchoring dossier puts at ~2 atlas px wide (not re-measured here).

dm_art_free_fit_context.note: Both optima sit on the search edge (s=0.5, dy +9..+10 S): coast shape alone pulls the chart smaller and south, the multimodal behaviour the dossier reported (0.32x / 0.55x / 1.01x modes). Coast chamfer cannot pick the policy scale.

verdicts.reference: Print mask and DEM shore are one coast to within 1.3-1.5 atlas px rms (p95 2.3-2.7, mainland max 5.4 near Epeshu). The DM chart is the outlier (8.5 px rms, 21 px max to the print under today's cityBox). Use the print mask as the registration target and seam clip (atlas authoritative); the DEM agrees with it and needs no reconciliation shift.
verdicts.street_handoff: After registration, the atlas shows the chart coast and the sim shows the DEM coast. At the best policy fit (0.6x, +3 E) art-to-DEM is 3.57 rms / 6.84 max atlas px = 646 / 1238 screen px at z11.5 (today 6.88 / 18.84 = 1245 / 3410). The jump is the chart-vs-atlas residual, not a DEM error: DEM-to-print is 1.33 rms. No medium change cures it; only fitting the chart, or cross-fading to the DEM/print coast at handoff, does. Caveats: assumes the H2z handoff maps atlas px to sim world by the same S1 formula with no error of its own (unverified; any handoff error adds to this jump), and uses the raw DEM, not genHydrology's carved W.H.
verdicts.b38: q08-c08's 'DEM shore 3.8-10.4 atlas px off the chart in the south' measured the DEM against the chart under today's cityBox. The DEM is not off the atlas; the chart is. Under a translate+scale override B-38's clip becomes clip-to-registered-chart, which still trims ~3.6 px rms of DEM relief (0.6x+3E) and fails both ways (art land over print sea 91 px2 and art sea over print land 75 px2). Clipping contours to the print mask matches the DEM to ~1.4 px.
verdicts.seam_both_signs: Today the chart puts land over atlas sea (666 px2, 26% of box) and never sea over land. Shrinking trades one sign for the other: 0.6x+3E 91/75 px2 (10%/8%), 0.6x+8E 39/107 (4%/12%), 0.8x+3E 212/35 (13%/2%). A clip against atlas water fixes only land-over-sea; sea-over-land needs the chart's own water class made transparent or replaced by the atlas sea.

reference_coasts_r60.note: atlas px; DEM 0 m contour (S1 vertex convention, sea-connected, raw decode) and print coast (buildCityMask port, raw, includes speck/islet holes) within 60 px of the Epeshu anchor
